review_text: Here’s a quick education on some fundamentals. It’s very worth the read. First, let’s define the terms: “Device size”: length from top to bottom of device itself. “Display size”: screen size measured diagonally, usually bigger than device size. Examples: S24 Ultra: 6.8 inch display, 6.39 inch device S24 Plus: 6.7 inch display, 6.24 inch device S24: 6.2 inch display, 5.79 inch device Conclusion: Device can be a half inch smaller than display without sacrificing anything. So why is the gap between display and device size in budget phones much less? Because of useless bezels i.e. dead space around the screen that just contributes to a bulkier device size for ABSOLUTELY NO REASON. The most egregious example is the A14 with a 6.6 display and 6.6 device size due to its gigantic bezels. Remove that dead space and you’re left with a more manageable 6.2 inch device. The A15 is somewhat better, but the gap is still 6.5 to 6.3. The A55/A35 are slightly better, with a gap of 6.6 to 6.34/6.37, but they can also be 6.2 inches. But will the battery fit? Well, the 6.23 inch A54 clearly shows a 5000 mAh battery fitting into 6.2 inches. So why are bezels added? To purposely stick it to budget customers! It’s not like the manufacturer has to go out of their way and do anything extra for budget customers, just DON’T ADD dead space! You may ask: “What’s a few tenths of an inch already?” Well guess what, the difference between a compact device and a big bulky one is often less than an inch. So in phones, every tenth of an inch makes a real difference. Weight is also a problem. As an example, the S24 Plus is 6.91 oz. So why is the A15 - 7.05 oz, the A14 - 7.13 oz, the A55 - very heavy at 7.37 oz, and the A35 - an astounding 7.51 oz! The A13 seems to manage just fine at 6.88 oz. And when you’re holding a phone for a while, you can bet that those ounces (or grams) add up to tire and/or hurt your hand! Bottom line: in addition to the discussion of producing actual compact phones that are affordable which should absolutely be done, today’s budget phones can be more manageable IN THEIR CURRENT FORM if their useless dead space and extra weight is removed.

review_text: I posted a comment recently about being disappointed with the graininess of the screen on my new S24 Ultra, in addition to the washed out colours. Just thought I'd provide an update, if anyone is interested! The network provider I purchased the phone from recommended going to one of their stores to get it booked in for repair assessment. The store staff member had a look at the phone and actually agreed with me that she could see the graininess. But after running the standard Samsung diagnostic didn't bring up any faults, she said there was really no point sending it to their own repair centre if it was more of a quality issue rather than an outright fault as they wouldn't be able to do anything. So she told me to speak to Samsung. Samsung did agree to take it in for repair due to the grain, after I sent a photo to confirm the issue. It's not Samsung themselves doing the repair but an 'authorised repairer'. They called me after a couple days saying their techs couldn't find a fault. I explained the issue and said it may be more of a quality control issue, but that I had directly compared my S24 Ultra unit to a display model in a local shop and that unit had far less grain on the screen. One of the salesmen in that shop saw me comparing the two and it turned out he was quite a techie like myself so was interested in the issue. He was also able to notice the screen on my unit looking grainier once we had matched the settings. So that's outright proof that the screen quality/graininess seems to be quite variable between units. I said to the repair centre advisor, if you just get your techs to Google the issue, they can easily see how to look out for it and what conditions it's worst in (i.e. low brightness, dark/grey colours displayed). They said they would pass that on to the techs and if they still couldn't find an issue, a 'quality control' department would check it. Well I got the phone back a few days ago with a report saying they couldn't find any faults and that everything was within Samsung's spec so they didn't do anything to it apart from update to latest software. Grain is still present on the screen. So definitely disappointed with Samsung. Gonna be selling the phone on now as the screen on my S22 Ultra looks a lot better. I think Samsung is really dropping the ball with their OLED quality control. Just had a new Asus laptop arrive a few days ago - a £2500 model - that has a Samsung manufactured OLED touchscreen and the screen on that is fucked out of the box. Has bright lines running across the middle of the screen, worse on darker colours but still noticeable on lots of content. And the colour tint is a lot warmer on the left hand side. Definitely seems to be a hardware issue as no updates (including BIOS/firmware) has changed it. Of course Asus should have caught that issue but it's a Samsung screen. So now gonna have to wait for that to be repaired. At least that's a very noticeable fault ( https://1drv.ms/i/s!AqHC9qx1s8H_hP8KBAMBFBDbAlXpag?e=1tD6lo if anyone wants a look) whereas the S24 Ultra issue is more subtle, but still frustrating when it's worst for the ways I use the phone i.e. low brightness with dark mode.

Also not liking the flat screen, it looks cheap and feels less comfortable to hold. I accept this is personal preference though and lots of people prefer that extra little bit of screen space or like it for writing with the S Pen. But personally it's a downgrade for me. The curved edges of the S22U just looked lovely and seamless, like the screen is floating in the air. And felt more comfortable for swipe gestures like the left swipe I have set up as the back action in Good Lock's One Hand Operation+.
